rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Domestic Violence Lease Termination
rules.quote: Within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant's security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant's agent.
rules.summary: When a tenant terminates their lease due to domestic violence under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest within 15 business days after the lease terminates.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to tenants terminating lease under Safe Housing Act; does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Service Members
rules.quote: The landlord is required to return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26).
rules.summary: When a service member terminates their lease under the Service Members Civil Relief Act, the landlord must return the security deposit in accordance with New Jersey's security deposit law.
rules.coverage_text: Applies when service member properly terminates lease under Service Members Civil Relief Act.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act - Good Cause Requirement for Lease Non-Renewal
rules.quote: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.summary: Landlords of residential rental properties must have good cause to refuse to renew a lease, with exceptions for owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings and transient or seasonal units.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to residential rental properties except owner-occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two or three family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units are exempt.

rules.title: No Discrimination Against Service/Guide Dog Owners
rules.quote: A handicapped, blind, or deaf person who has a service or guide dog, or who obtains a service or guide dog, shall have full and equal access to all housing accommodations and shall not be required to pay extra compensation. Any lease or rental agreement prohibiting pets shall not apply to a service or guide dog owned by a handicapped, blind, or deaf tenant.
rules.summary: Landlords cannot discriminate against handicapped, blind, or deaf tenants who have service or guide dogs, and pet prohibitions in leases do not apply to service or guide dogs.

rules.title: Eviction Stay for Service Members
rules.quote: Moreover, if the rent does not exceed $3,991.90 per month, eviction actions may be stayed by the courts for three (3) months unless the court finds that the tenant's ability to pay rent is not materially affected by reason of the military service.
rules.summary: Courts may stay eviction actions for three months for service members whose rent does not exceed $3,991.90 per month (as of 2020, adjusted annually), unless military service did not materially affect their ability to pay rent.
rules.coverage_text: Applies when rent does not exceed $3,991.90 per month (2020 amount, increases annually with CPI housing component).

rules.title: Maximum security deposit limit
rules.quote: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month's rent
rules.summary: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit that exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.penalty: If tenant is successful in suit, court may award double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees per N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1. Civil penalty of $500-$2,000 for willful withholding from assisted tenants per N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.5. Criminal charge as disorderly person, fine not less than $200 or imprisonment not more than 30 days for unlawful use per N.J.S.A. 46:8-25.

rules.title: Return of security deposit after tenancy termination
rules.quote: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.summary: A landlord must return the tenant's security deposit plus interest, minus any lawful deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.penalty: If tenant is successful in suit, court may award double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Return of security deposit after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation
rules.quote: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.
rules.summary: When a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation and an official prohibits occupancy or certifies displacement longer than seven days, the landlord must return the security deposit within five business days.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.penalty: If tenant is successful in suit, court may award double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibition
rules.quote: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.summary: Landlords are prohibited from discriminating against tenants based on their source of lawful income when renting housing.
rules.coverage_text: The law applies to all landlord-tenant relationships, except those involving two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.
rules.exemption_note: Exempt for two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in owner or resident-occupied single homes, and single-sex residences like YMCA and age-restricted housing (familial status only).
rules.penalty: Landlords who violate this law are subject to substantial fines and penalties, up to $10,000 for a first offense per N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a). May be required to pay monetary damages and rent the unit to the complainant.

rules.title: Exemption for newly constructed multiple dwellings from local rent control
rules.quote: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: This is an exemption from local rent control for newly constructed buildings for 30 years.

rules.title: Notice requirements for rent increase eviction under Anti-Eviction Act
rules.quote: This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.summary: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, a landlord must serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase, and the increase must not be unconscionable.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirement
rules.quote: A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction. In an eviction action, when a landlord obtains a judgment of possession of the unit from a court, the landlord is entitled to a warrant for removal.
rules.summary: A landlord may only recover possession of a residential dwelling unit by tenant consent or through the legal eviction process.
rules.coverage_text: dwelling unit used as a residence

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Notice to Quit Requirement
rules.quote: A 'Notice to Quit' is required for all good cause evictions, except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). A 'Notice to Quit' is a notice given by the landlord terminating the tenancy and ordering the tenant to vacate the premises.
rules.summary: A Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent cases.
rules.exemption_note: Exception for nonpayment of rent evictions

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirement for Eviction or Non-Renewal
rules.quote: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause eviction. Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant.
rules.summary: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant and must describe the cause in detail in a written notice, except for nonpayment of rent.

rules.title: Landlord Registration Requirement - Eviction Prohibition
rules.quote: The landlord registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37).
rules.summary: A landlord is prohibited from evicting a tenant if the landlord has not been properly registered.
rules.coverage_text: one or two-family non-owner-occupied home and buildings with three or more units
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied two-family homes are exempt from registration requirement
rules.penalty: $500.00 maximum penalty for each offense under N.J.S.A. 46:8-35

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirements
rules.quote: The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes.
rules.summary: Landlords in New Jersey can only evict tenants for good cause as enumerated in the Anti-Eviction Act, which applies to most residential rental properties.
rules.coverage_text: This law may not apply to two - or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units. It does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant.
rules.exemption_note: May not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-unit properties with two or fewer rental units; does not apply to transient hotel/motel guests or seasonal tenants in guest houses.

rules.title: Warrant for Possession Timeline
rules.quote: The warrant for possession may not be issued until three (3) business days after the judgment for possession is granted. The tenant has three (3) business days to move all persons and belongings from the premises.
rules.summary: After a judgment for possession, a warrant for possession cannot be issued until three business days have passed, and the tenant then has three business days to vacate after service of the warrant.

rules.title: Stay of Eviction for Special Circumstances
rules.quote: A tenant may ask the court for permission to stay in the premises due to special circumstances that moving may cause. This action is a stay of eviction. If permission is granted, the tenant may not stay in the premises for more than one year, unless there is an agreed upon extension between landlord and tenant.
rules.summary: A tenant may request a court-ordered stay of eviction due to special circumstances for up to one year unless the landlord and tenant agree to an extension.

rules.title: Self-Help Eviction Prohibition
rules.quote: A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant's belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant
rules.summary: Landlords cannot evict tenants by force or lockout without a court order and may be liable for damages if they attempt a self-help eviction.
rules.penalty: In a successful action by a tenant evicted through forcible entry and detainer, the court may award possession of the dwelling unit and all damages, including court costs and reasonable attorney fees.

rules.title: Eviction for Nonpayment of Rent - Notice Requirement for Subsidized Housing
rules.quote: The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. If the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite for eviction
rules.summary: Landlords may file an eviction suit for nonpayment of rent without prior notice except in federally subsidized housing, where a 14-day notice is required.

rules.title: Eviction for Disorderly Conduct - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction
rules.summary: A landlord may evict for disorderly conduct after giving a written Notice to Cease and serving a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing suit.

rules.title: Eviction for Damage to Property - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction
rules.summary: Tenants who intentionally or through gross negligence damage property may be evicted after receiving a Notice to Quit at least three days before suit is filed.

rules.title: Eviction for Violation of Rules - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: If after given a written Notice to Cease violating or breaching reasonable rules and regulations contained in the lease or accepted in writing by the tenant, the tenant continues to substantially violate or breach the rules and regulations, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction.
rules.summary: A landlord may evict for continued substantial breach of reasonable rules after giving a Notice to Cease and a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit, with notices given on or before the start of a new month.

rules.title: Eviction for Failure to Pay Rent Increase
rules.quote: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction
rules.summary: A tenant may be evicted for refusing to pay a rent increase that is not unconscionable and complies with rent control laws, after receiving a Notice to Quit at least one month before suit is filed.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Illegal Occupancy Eviction
rules.quote: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent. The landlord is responsible for paying the tenant's relocation expenses.
rules.summary: Tenants evicted due to illegal occupancy are entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times their monthly rent, which the landlord must pay at least five days before removal.
rules.penalty: If not paid timely and no municipal fund exists, interest accrues at 18% per year and the amount becomes a lien on the property.

rules.title: Eviction for Permanent Retirement from Residential Use - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.
rules.summary: A landlord may evict to permanently retire property from residential use after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing suit, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.

rules.title: Eviction for Refusal to Accept Lease Changes - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the terms and conditions of the lease. If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing suit for eviction
rules.summary: A landlord may evict when a lease expires if the tenant refuses reasonable changes to lease terms, after giving written notice and serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit.

rules.title: Eviction for Habitual Late Rent Payment - Notice Requirement
rules.quote: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction
rules.summary: A landlord may evict for habitual late rent payment after giving a Notice to Cease and serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit.

rules.title: Eviction for Conversion to Condominium - Notice Requirement and Stay
rules.quote: If the landlord or owner of a building or mobile home park is converting the property from the rental market to a condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more dwelling units or park sites, except as hereinafter provided in subsection (L) below, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.
rules.summary: A landlord converting property to condominium or cooperative ownership may evict tenants after serving a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing suit, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.exemption_note: Up to five one-year stays of eviction may be granted if tenant has not been offered comparable housing; not more than one-year stay if landlord allows five months' free rent. No action permitted against senior citizen or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status.

rules.title: Eviction After Conversion - Owner Occupancy (Post-Recording Tenancy)
rules.quote: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building or mobile home park, which is constructed as or being converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, seeks to evict a tenant or sublessee whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, or agreement establishing the cooperative or subdivision plat was recorded, because the owner has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction.
rules.summary: An owner may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the condominium or cooperative conversion was recorded if the owner has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who will personally occupy it, after serving a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing suit.

rules.title: Eviction for Employment Termination
rules.quote: If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction
rules.summary: A landlord may evict a tenant whose residence is conditioned on employment by the landlord, after serving a Notice to Quit three days before filing suit.

rules.title: Eviction for Drug Conviction on Property
rules.quote: The landlord may file a suit for eviction, if the tenant, including juveniles who have been found by the Court to be delinquent, has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses that took place on the property, and has not in connection with his sentence either (1) successfully completed or (2) been admitted to and continues during probation participation toward completion of a drug rehabilitation program. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction
rules.summary: A landlord may evict a tenant convicted of or pleading guilty to drug offenses on the property who has not successfully completed or is not participating in drug rehabilitation, after serving a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing suit.
rules.exemption_note: No eviction suit may be brought more than two years after the juvenile was found delinquent, the person was convicted, or after release from incarceration, whichever is later.

rules.title: Owner-Occupied Two- and Three-Family Dwelling Evictions
rules.quote: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant (a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent, (c) is disorderly so as to destroy the peace and quiet of other tenants, (d) willfully destroys or damages the premises, (e) constantly violates the written rules and regulations or (f) violates any lease provision where the lease reserves a right of re-entry for such violations.
rules.summary: In owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings, tenants may only be evicted by court order for enumerated causes including lease expiration, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, rule violations, or lease violations.

rules.title: Prohibition on Retaliatory Eviction
rules.quote: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights
rules.summary: Landlords are prohibited from retaliatory eviction or lease alteration when tenants exercise civil rights such as enforcing lease rights, making good faith complaints to authorities about health or safety violations, or joining tenant organizations.
rules.coverage_text: all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.exemption_note: Does not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.penalty: If a landlord does take reprisal action, the tenant may sue the landlord for damages in a civil action.

rules.title: Penalty for False Owner-Occupancy Eviction
rules.quote: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months. If instead the landlord permits personal occupancy of the unit by another tenant or registration of conversion of the property to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs
rules.summary: If a tenant vacates after receiving notice of landlord's personal occupancy and the landlord fails to occupy the unit for at least six months, the landlord is liable for three times damages plus attorney fees.
rules.penalty: Three times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs.

rules.title: Penalty for False Permanent Retirement Eviction
rules.quote: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years. If the landlord allows any residential use of the unit during the five (5) year period from the date the unit became vacant, the landlord, or the former landlord, may be liable to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs. Additionally, the landlord or former landlord may be liable for a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation of this law
rules.summary: If a tenant vacates after notice of permanent retirement from residential use and the landlord uses the property residentially within five years, the landlord is liable for three times damages plus attorney fees and a civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.
rules.penalty: Three times the damages plus attorney fees and costs, and a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation.

rules.title: Tenant Notice and Protections in Foreclosure - 90-Day Notice
rules.quote: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90-day notice to quit when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.
rules.summary: A tenant in a foreclosed property must receive a 90-day notice to quit if the new buyer intends to personally occupy the property as a primary residence, and no action may be taken until any existing lease expires.
rules.exemption_note: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirement.

rules.title: Post-Foreclosure Tenant Notification Requirement
rules.quote: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to move because of the foreclosure.
rules.summary: The new owner of a foreclosed property must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale that ownership has changed and that they are not required to move due to the foreclosure.

rules.title: Prohibition on Pressure Tactics in Foreclosure Buyout Offers
rules.quote: Pursuant to the New Jersey Foreclosure Fairness Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-69 et seq.), pressure tactics include but are not limited to (N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b)): 1. Mischaracterizing or misrepresenting the rights of the tenant under the law; 2. Implying the tenant is obligated to accept the offer; 3. Implying that there will be consequences against the tenant for failing to accept the offer; 4. Harassment, including but not limited to discontinuance of utilities, failure to maintain common areas or facilities, or any other failure to maintain the premises in a habitable condition; and 5. An increase in rent in excess of any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or if the property is not subject to rent control, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.
rules.summary: Under the Foreclosure Fairness Act, pressure tactics to force tenants to accept buyout offers are prohibited, including misrepresenting tenant rights, implying obligation, harassment, utility shutoffs, and unreasonable rent increases.
